article.title: How Long Do Opened Spirits Last?
article.body:
How Long Do Opened Spirits Last?

An unopened bottle of spirits keeps indefinitely if stored upright away from heat and light. Once opened, whisky, gin, vodka, rum and tequila stay safe to drink, but Drinks House 247 suggests finishing them within one to two years, because air slowly fades the aroma, and faster once the bottle is less than a third full.

Spirits do not go off in the way wine, beer or milk do. Their high alcohol content, usually 37.5% to 40% ABV or more, stops bacteria and moulds from growing, so an opened bottle will not make anyone ill. What does change is the flavour. Over months and years, an opened bottle loses some of what made it worth buying.

What happens to a spirit once it is opened?

Two things. First, oxidation: the air that enters the bottle slowly reacts with aroma compounds, flattening the brighter notes. Second, evaporation: every time the cap comes off, a little alcohol and aroma escape. Neither happens quickly, but both accelerate as the level in the bottle drops, because there is more air in contact with less liquid. This empty space at the top of the bottle is called headspace.

How long does each spirit last once opened?

Spirit Best within, once opened What fades first
VodkaYears; changes very littleVery little to lose
GinAbout 1 to 2 yearsFresh citrus and floral botanicals
Blanco tequilaAbout 1 to 2 yearsBright, peppery agave notes
Aged tequila, rum and brandyAbout 1 to 2 yearsTop notes; the oak character lasts longer
WhiskyAbout 1 to 2 years if more than half fullDelicate fruit and floral aromas; smoke lasts well
Cream liqueursFollow the labelDairy content can spoil; keep cool
Vermouth and fortified winesAbout 1 to 2 months, in the fridgeFreshness; it oxidises like wine

These are guides for flavour, not safety. A bottle opened three years ago is still safe; it may simply taste flatter than it did.

Why does a nearly empty bottle fade faster?

A full bottle has only a small pocket of air. A bottle with a few centimetres left has a large one, so the remaining spirit is exposed to far more oxygen. A whisky that tasted the same for a year at three-quarters full can change noticeably within months once it is down to its last quarter. If you have a special bottle in that state, the best option is to drink it, or pour it into a smaller bottle that it fills to the top.

How should you store opened spirits?

  • Upright. Unlike wine, spirits should stand. High-strength alcohol can slowly damage a cork that is kept wet.
  • Sealed tightly. Replace the cap or cork straight after pouring. Pourer spouts left in a bottle let aroma escape constantly.
  • Out of the light. Sunlight can fade colour and change flavour, especially in clear glass.
  • Somewhere cool and steady. Around 15 to 20°C, away from radiators, ovens and sunny windows.

Do corks fail?

Natural corks in spirits bottles can dry out and crumble over many years, particularly if the bottle is stored in a warm room. If a cork breaks, strain the spirit through a clean coffee filter to remove any fragments and move it to a bottle with a screw cap or a spare stopper. The spirit itself is unaffected.

Does whisky keep improving in the bottle?

No. Whisky and other aged spirits only develop while they are in the cask, where wood and air work on them over years. Once bottled, they stop ageing. A 12-year-old whisky bottled in 2010 is still a 12-year-old whisky today. Unopened, it will taste much as it did on release; opened, it will slowly lose aroma.

How can you tell if a spirit has faded?

Compare it with your memory of the first pour, or with a fresh bottle if you have one. Signs of fading include a muted nose, a thinner texture and a shorter finish. If you notice a sour, musty or cardboard-like smell, the cork may have been tainted; that is unpleasant but not harmful.

Practical tips for a home bar

  • Open bottles you will actually drink, and finish them before opening another of the same kind.
  • Keep vermouth in the fridge and buy smaller bottles; stale vermouth ruins Martinis and Negronis.
  • For rare bottles you want to make last, decant a portion into a small sample bottle to share or keep.

Frequently asked questions

Do spirits go off once opened?

Not in a harmful way. Their high alcohol content prevents spoilage. But opened spirits slowly lose aroma and flavour, so most are best within one to two years.

How long does opened whisky last?

About one to two years if the bottle is more than half full. Once it is down to the last quarter or so, the flavour can fade within months.

Does gin go bad after opening?

Gin stays safe to drink, but its fresh citrus and floral notes fade over time. Aim to finish an opened bottle within one to two years.

Should opened spirits be stored upright?

Yes. Store spirits upright, tightly sealed, away from light and heat. High-strength alcohol can damage a cork kept in constant contact with it.

article.summary: Sealed spirits keep indefinitely. Once opened, expect one to two years before flavour fades, sooner as the bottle empties. Why air matters and how to slow it.
